recommended_new_rule:
Freeze the previous executed occupancy and each user previous association before processing any request. Clear only transmissions whose beam is disabled in the CURRENT exogenous plan; do not insert any current requested or admitted transmission.
For a candidate on the previous serving satellite, use the user own previous valid subband. For any other satellite, use the lowest-index subband not occupied in its previous snapshot, with indices 0..9. If none exists, use subband0 only as a reference measurement for graph preselection/features and record q_choice_reason=full_satellite_reference; the candidate remains capacity-infeasible and cannot borrow that occupied band for execution.
Candidate SINR excludes the evaluated user own previous transmission, a declared hypothetical-release convention shared by all methods. All other interference uses frozen occupancy, current geometry/antenna angles and current exogenous attenuation. No future load, current admission order, or executed state is used.
Each candidate measurement uses receive boresight toward THAT candidate satellite. All interferers in that candidate SINR are evaluated relative to the same boresight. These are alternative beamformed measurements; actual data transmission uses only the finally selected link.

recommended_new_rule:
Keep source reservations through the epoch whenever the serving pair lies in D_k. A request rejected at its target can use this reserved source.
Before admitting new external users, a same-satellite feasible beam change retains its old subband and consumes no extra satellite slot. If the old pair itself is infeasible but the requested pair on the same satellite is feasible, explicitly give this existing user same-satellite priority and retain its old band; this boundary case must be recorded as a new-rule choice if historical behavior is unknown.
New external requests are ranked by decreasing frozen target SINR, breaking exact/tolerance-declared ties by ascending user ID. Each admitted request receives the smallest free subband index. A reservation released by an outbound handover is not reused during this epoch.
The capacity stage yields one tentative transmitting link per user: admitted target, retained source, or outage. Source and target never transmit simultaneously for one user. Reserved but inactive source resources consume admission capacity but create no interference.

recommended_new_rule:
One simultaneous physical check only. Freeze all tentative assignments/subbands and boresights, calculate visibility and SINR jointly, and mark every failing link.
Delete all failing transmissions together. No second admission round, no reallocation of released subbands, no second attempt at a source after the physical check. Admission-rejection source fallback occurs BEFORE this check and is checked like every other tentative link.
Recompute final interference and rates for survivors without changing their subbands, boresights, signal power, or exogenous attenuation. The removed links may become physically feasible after interference removal, but remain unserved for this epoch.
Under these rules the survivor final SINR cannot be below its check SINR, apart from rounding. A violation identifies a resource/power/pointing change or a coding inconsistency.

recommended_new_rule:
Before controller evaluation, freeze 500 potential ground planning locations sampled by the paper location law. Use nested subsets for K=100..500. Treat these locations as known external deployment/planning inputs and never select them using controller outcomes.
At each 20 s boundary, for each satellite form eligible planning targets whose geometric elevation is at least 25 deg. A target covers a planning point for planning purposes if the angular separation of the satellite-to-point and satellite-to-target directions is at most 1 deg.
Greedily select the target covering the greatest number of still-uncovered eligible planning points; ties use increasing planning point ID. Remove only the covered points from the planning objective. Stop after seven distinct targets or no positive coverage. Enable the first four positive-coverage targets, or all if fewer than four.
Match new targets to prior beam IDs by minimum total angular distance using directions seen from the CURRENT satellite position. Break equal-cost matchings lexicographically by beam ID and target ID; allocate unused IDs in ascending order. At the first interval use selection order.
Hold Earth-fixed targets for 20 s; recompute the satellite-to-target pointing vector every second. The 1 deg planning radius is not an additional service cutoff: geometric visibility, antenna gain, physical SINR and satellite capacity determine actual service.
Save the full target and enable trajectory and reuse it for all methods and all K. Do not use current association, learned score, admission result, executed load, future random weather or future random channel values.

For a new minimal model, draw one Bernoulli(0.10) rain state PER USER per episode. Keep it through all 800 epochs; share it across all satellite/beam paths received by that user. Draw different users independently. Use nested user IDs so density scans reuse the same user weather.
Draw one blockage Markov chain PER USER, independent across users and independent of rain, and share its state across all links to that user. Initialize from the stationary probability 0.005263/(0.1+0.005263); use the paper transitions once per second.
Apply the receiving user atmospheric/rain/blockage attenuation to both desired and interfering paths. This user-local common attenuation is an explicit simplified spatial-correlation assumption, not a claim that it matches the historical generator.
Share the entire exogenous weather realization across methods.
